 The University of Montana Grizzlies have little time to savor Eli Gillman’s latest milestone. The Grizzlies return to Washington-Grizzly Stadium on Saturday to face Idaho State in a matchup that could shape both teams’ postseason chances.
 The game is UM’s final home contest of the regular season and Senior Day for 22 Grizzlies. Montana is 7-3 overall and 5-2 in Big Sky Conference play, with a trip to Montana State still ahead. Idaho State is 6-4 and 3-4 in conference play.
 “There’s always emotion playing in every game, especially when you’re at home,” Montana coach Bobby Kennedy said. “And you’re right, ESPN2, probably another sellout at Washington-Grizzly, Senior Day, it’s a special day. But the thing guys have to remember is it’s not their last game.”
 The Grizzlies come in riding a two game winning streak. Last week, Gillman rushed for 196 yards and four touchdowns in a 57-24 win over Portland State, setting a Big Sky career record with his 78th total touchdown. He also tied Montana’s single game record with four touchdowns. A week earlier, Montana beat Eastern Washington 41-14 and set a program record with 11 sacks.
 Gillman and quarterback Keali’i Ah Yat lead an offense averaging 40.1 points and 488.9 yards per game, both among the Big Sky’s best. Ah Yat has thrown for 2,866 yards and 27 touchdowns, while Brooks Davis leads Montana with 81 catches for 1,233 yards and 12 touchdowns.
 Idaho State will test the Grizzlies through the air. The Bengals average 283.4 passing yards per game, and quarterback Jordan Cooke threw for 318 yards in a 28-26 triple overtime loss to Montana State last week. Idaho State outgained the defending national champions 410-332, showing it can challenge a highly ranked opponent even in defeat.
 Montana cornerback Sage Salopek said the Grizzlies are preparing for that challenge.
 “It’s definitely exciting. We’ll be ready for it. We just got to be ready, follow Coach Eric’s plan and be ready for the challenge,” Salopek said.
 The Bengals also bring a defense that leads the Big Sky with 61 tackles for loss and has allowed just 191.6 passing yards per game. Montana’s offensive line has allowed only nine sacks this season, the fewest in the conference. Protecting Ah Yat and keeping the Bengals from disrupting the backfield will be key as the Grizzlies try to keep their offense moving.
 The postseason stakes are real for both teams. A win would move Montana to 8-3 and strengthen its playoff case before the regular season finale at Montana State. Idaho State needs a win to keep its own playoff hopes alive; a loss would leave the Bengals at 6-5 and 3-5 in conference play. Neither team can treat Saturday as a postseason guarantee, but the result could make the path clearer or much narrower.
 Montana leads the all time series 49-13 and has won 16 straight meetings. The Grizzlies are 19-0 against Idaho State at Washington-Grizzly Stadium. Last season, Montana rallied from a 13 point deficit to win 46-38 in Pocatello.
 Kickoff is scheduled for Saturday at 8:30 p.m. at Washington-Grizzly Stadium.
